Hi Kate — thanks for the details and the heads-up on timelines. Attaching our latest rate card and a short modeling workbook that maps token bands to net unit costs after standard volume discounts. High-level answers below to get you started:

- Baseline (hosted API, gen/chat): $0.0045 per 1K tokens for baseline text-gen; embeddings are $0.0009 per 1K tokens.
- Tiering suggestion (examples):
  * 0–10B: list rate (no discount)
  * 10B–50B: 12% discount off list
  * 50B–200B: 24% discount off list
  * >200B: custom negotiation (typically additional incremental discount + reserved commit model)
- Minimum commit: optional; we recommend a 3–6 month commit to access deeper discounts and burst protection.
- Burst: hosted customers can burst beyond committed capacity subject to soft throttles; sustained overage triggers a short-term overage rate or an auto-upgrade recommendation.
- SLA credits: standard for Dedicated; hosted API includes uptime SLO and token processing latency targets — we provide credits on a case-by-case basis for sustained SLA misses.

I attached: redwood_rate_card_v3.pdf and q3_volume_model.xlsx. The workbook has two workload scenarios prefilled (conversational vs. batch embeddings) that map to the tier bands.

Would you like a short walk-through (15–20 min) with Marcus from pricing/SE to align the model to your prompt mix? If procurement wants final numbers we can convert the ranges into a formal commercial worksheet.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Kate — looping in a couple of product/pricing clarifications so we can tighten the numbers before your procurement review:

A few specifics we usually confirm:
- Token mix: what percent is short-chat (<256 tokens) vs. long-form generation (>1k)? Aggregated effective tokens can materially change the cost profile.
- Embedding cadence: batch (daily/hourly) vs. streaming; batch jobs often get a lower effective cost if scheduled and cached.
- KV cache opportunity: if you have repeat prompt prefixes we can advise on prefix caching which reduces billable tokens.

Operational notes:
- For 50B+ bands, we typically propose a blended per-token rate in the commercial worksheet instead of a hard list/discount formula; that avoids cliff effects during month-to-month variability.
- If you expect fast month-over-month growth, we can set a rolling 30-day average to determine applied tier for billing rather than peak usage.

If you can share a 2‑week sample of request logs (anonymized) we can produce a tailored cost estimate and an applied tier recommendation. Happy to run that with Neha and Vanessa.

Thanks — Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
